excerpt: Transcribes recorded audio and video asynchronously across 99 languages, with support on speaker diarization, PII redaction, and more features.
Handles live audio over WebSocket with ~150ms p50 latency, powering voice agents, live captions, and real-time agent-assist tools in contact centers.
Transcribes audio up to 20 minutes long over HTTP ... in a single request-response call — no polling or webhooks needed.
You include formatting instructions with your audio, and the transcript comes back already cleaned up and formatted.
Layers speech analysis on top of transcripts — summarization, sentiment, topic detection, and more over audio — for extracting structured insight.
Provides safety, privacy, and compliance controls — PII handling, content moderation, and related safeguards
Gives unified access to frontier language models through the same API, so teams can apply reasoning models to their transcription without a separate integration.
Use the Python or TypeScript SDK to integrate transcription, streaming, and voice agents directly into your own codebase.
Drop AssemblyAI into existing voice-agent frameworks and platforms — LiveKit, Pipecat, Twilio, Langflow, and others.
Add a one-liner to your AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or .cursorrules so your agent refetches the latest integration prompt before every AssemblyAI prompt
Docs MCP server ... Devs whose agent does heavy mid-session doc lookups.
You want curated SDK-specific context (Python / JS / streaming / voice agents) bundled with the agent, auto-loaded when relevant.
Narrow with ?lang=python or ?lang=typescript to save tokens, or add ?excludeSpec=true to skip the API reference.
Contextual prompting capabilities; Keyterms prompting up to 1,000 words
for anything outside that set, the system automatically falls back to Universal-2, giving you coverage across 99 languages total without any extra configuration.
Medical Mode (domain: "medical-v1") is an add-on that enhances transcription accuracy for medical terminology — including medication names, procedures, conditions, and dosages.
Prefer to try it first? Transcribe audio without writing any code in the AssemblyAI Playground.
The SDK uploads, submits, and polls for you in a single call.
Speaker diarization identifies individual speakers in your audio and labels each segment of the transcript with the speaker.
The AssemblyAI SDK manages the WebSocket connection and session termination for you.
Transcribe a team meeting with speaker labels, identify speakers by name, then generate structured meeting notes with LLM Gateway.
Set up SAML or OIDC Single Sign-On for your AssemblyAI organization, including step-by-step configuration for Okta, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Entra ID.
opt out of the model improvement program, set a time-to-live for audio and transcripts, and sign a BAA, all self-serve from the dashboard.
Your users speak, and it returns text that is ready to send: filler gone, self-corrections resolved, names spelled right.

A user integrating Google's speech API compared outputs. Google: "There is a multiloculated fluid collection adjacent to the liver." AssemblyAI: "There is a multi located fluid collection..." Google does better out of the box, but AssemblyAI is customizable to a medical vocabulary, which Google isn't. The user says AssemblyAI needs real-time dictation, the major need in medicine.

Critic: the claim of "the world's most advanced Speech-to-Text" is a very bold statement, with no blog post explaining which technique is used, so it is hard to sell. Several commenters asked for WER benchmarks (LibriSpeech, TED) and found none.
The polling loop in the example screenshot doesn't seem a very nice thing to do to their servers.
Pricing complaint: by one user's math, volume discounts are only offered if you are spending about $130k annually.
Privacy concern: the privacy policy says customer audio, which may contain users' personally identifiable information, is used to provide and improve services and "for training purposes."

Skeptic of the launch claim that a custom TensorFlow model makes things more affordable than Kaldi or Sphinx: "Kaldi and Sphinx are far more efficient than any tensorflow transcription model I've ever seen."
Praise: "Was excited to see AssemblyAI is free for open-source projects."

Website issues reported at launch: the pricing page contained no pricing information, the CTA buttons near the bottom overlapped on mobile, and the Basic and Enterprise email links on the pricing page had swapped subject lines.
"Your pricing seems on par with google and ibm."

A user who wants to transcribe old speeches and radio shows full of "terms of art" welcomed the customization. They had "been wanting something like this for years" because no one at Google would tell them how to train Google's API for their use case.

Critic: it appears to be a slightly tweaked CTC architecture in TensorFlow marketed as novel in-house tech. There are no WER benchmarks to compare with other APIs, yet the pricing is the same. Adding new words without LM data is not as flawless as claimed. "I'm still a bit confused why somebody would use AssemblyAI over other APIs given the same price."
